output.myth: Ithúna went down to the Skarel rocks one grey morning after the goats, and the sea took her before anyone saw. Her mother could not bury what she had not been given back, so she made a kite of her daughter's sailcloth, bone-stiffened and painted with the girl's mark, and she flew it off the highest cliff. Hesk, who keeps count of every string, watched the line run out and did not tie it off. Then the string parted, as strings do, and the kite went up past the Gulls and the weather into the Unflown, where no tale says it has come down. Tavo laughed when he saw it, and would not give it back. Her mother still stands on the rocks at dusk, hands open, tugging at nothing. Sil, the Drowned Lantern, is sure she has seen the kite once, far south, and each new moon she goes looking for it too.
output.verse:
Cut string, the kite rides
her mother hauls on nothing
still she looks for it
